Task: implement the real Crustdata provider. Create ONLY src/core/data/crustdata-provider.ts, tests/crustdata-provider.test.ts and scripts/crustdata-smoke.ts. Touch nothing else. Never read .env or print environment variables, headers or keys. Tests must make NO network calls (inject a fake fetch). No new dependencies. First read src/core/types.ts, src/core/data/provider.ts, fixture-provider.ts and tests/fixture-provider.test.ts, and mirror the FixtureProvider's semantics (BudgetGuard before the call, partial enrich results, no_match when nothing matches).

CrustdataProvider implements CompanyProvider. Constructor options, all explicit (never read process.env inside the provider): api_key, budget: BudgetGuard, base_url (default https://api.crustdata.com), fetch (default global fetch), timeout_ms (default 30000), max_retries (default 2). Headers on every call: Content-Type application/json, Authorization Bearer <key>, x-api-version 2025-11-01.

Endpoints and shapes (verified on our account):
1. autocompleteIndustry(query): POST /company/search/autocomplete body {"field":"taxonomy.professional_network_industry","query":query,"limit":10}; response {"suggestions":[{"value":string}]}; return the values. Free (cost 0), outside the caps.
2. searchCompanies(filters, limit): POST /company/search. Body: {"filters":{"op":"and","conditions":[ {"field":"locations.country","type":"=","value":country} (only when country is non-empty), {"field":"taxonomy.professional_network_industry","type":"in","value":industries} (only when non-empty), {"field":"basic_info.employee_count_range","type":"in","value":employee_count_ranges} (only when non-empty) ]},"sorts":[{"field":"basic_info.name","order":"asc"}],"fields":["crustdata_company_id","basic_info.logo_permalink","basic_info.name","basic_info.primary_domain","basic_info.website","basic_info.professional_network_url","basic_info.employee_count_range","taxonomy.professional_network_industry"],"limit":limit}. If there are no conditions, omit "filters". SEARCH RESPONSE PATHS (from our real call): <<PASTE THE paths.js OUTPUT FOR THE SEARCH RESPONSE HERE>>. Map each result to RawCompany with source "search".
3. enrichCompanies(linkedin_urls): POST /company/enrich body {"fields":["basic_info","headcount","locations","taxonomy"],"professional_network_profile_urls":[...]}; at most 25 URLs per HTTP call (chunk larger requests, each chunk checked by the budget guard first). The response is an ARRAY, one element per input URL: each element has matched_on (string), match_type (string), and matches[] whose items have confidence_score (number) and company_data with: crustdata_company_id (number); basic_info.{name, primary_domain, website, professional_network_url, employee_count_range, description, company_type, year_founded (number|null), logo_permalink, status}; headcount.total (number|null); locations.{city, state, country, street_address, headquarters, all_office_addresses[]}; taxonomy.{professional_network_industry (string), professional_network_specialities (string[])}. All other paths exist but must be ignored. For each element take the highest-confidence match; an empty matches[] means no match for that URL. Map to RawCompany with source "enrich": name, primary_domain, website, professional_network_url, employee_count_range, industry (taxonomy.professional_network_industry), logo (logo_permalink), description, legal_type (company_type), founded_year (year_founded, null -> omit), latest_headcount (headcount.total, null -> omit), location {city, state, country} ONLY, specialities. NEVER copy street_address, headquarters or all_office_addresses anywhere. Missing or null fields become "" for required string fields or are omitted for optional ones; never throw on missing fields. revenue_range stays unset (the revenue group is not requested).

Errors: map to the existing ProviderError categories. 401/403 -> auth_failed; 429 -> rate_limited (retry up to max_retries with waits of 1s then 2s, honouring a Retry-After header if present, then return rate_limited); 400/422 -> bad_request; network errors, aborts, timeouts and 5xx -> timeout (retry the same way); an enrich call where nothing matched -> no_match; if some URLs matched, return ok with the matched records only, like FixtureProvider. Error messages must be short and generic: status code and category only, never the response body, the URL list or any header.

Cost: export constants CRUSTDATA_PRICE_PER_SEARCH_RECORD_USD = 0.069 and CRUSTDATA_PRICE_PER_ENRICHED_COMPANY_USD = 0.60 with a comment that they are measured on our account (Oct 10-11, 2026, five measurements) and that unmatched enrichments are assumed free (unverified). Search cost = 0.069 x records returned; enrich cost = 0.60 x companies matched; autocomplete 0. Use BudgetGuard exactly as FixtureProvider does: refuse with budget_cap_reached BEFORE any fetch when canSearch(limit) or canEnrich(count) is false, and record spend after a successful call.

Tests (fake fetch, synthetic invented responses with exactly these paths and invented values, no real company data): mapping for search and enrich, street_address and all_office_addresses never appear in any output, highest confidence match chosen, partial and empty enrich results, 401, 429 retry then success, 429 exhausted, 5xx -> timeout, 400, budget refusal means fetch is never called, cost arithmetic, chunking of 30 URLs into 25 + 5, the API key never appears in any error message, and null or missing fields never throw.

scripts/crustdata-smoke.ts: a live smoke test. It requires --confirm-spend (otherwise it exits before any network call), reads the key from process.env.CRUSTDATA_API_KEY and passes it explicitly. It uses a BudgetGuard with max_search_results 3 and max_enrichments 1, calls autocompleteIndustry("staffing"), searchCompanies for India with that industry and sizes 11-50 and 51-200 (limit 3), then enriches ONE company from the search results that has a LinkedIn URL. It prints ONLY counts, costs and, per RawCompany field, how many records had it non-empty. It must never print names, domains, URLs or addresses. Expected live cost is about 0.81 dollars.

Run npx vitest run, npx tsc --noEmit and npm run lint. Do NOT run the smoke script. Summarise in 8 bullets, including anything you were unsure about.

content.text:
The Crustdata provider is written, and the full suite passes: vitest (192 tests, 13 files), `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` are all clean. I didn't run the smoke script.

- **Files:** I created only `src/core/data/crustdata-provider.ts`, `tests/crustdata-provider.test.ts` and `scripts/crustdata-smoke.ts`. The tests use a fake fetch, so they make no network calls, and the provider never reads `process.env`.
- **Search response paths:** the `<<PASTE THE paths.js OUTPUT…>>` placeholder in your task was never filled in, so I guessed the search response shape. The mapper takes a bare array, or one under `companies`, `results` or `data`. It reads each field as nested (`basic_info.name`) and falls back to a flat dotted key. Missing fields become `""`. Please check this against your real `paths.js` output before the live run.
- **Mirrors FixtureProvider:** the budget guard is checked before any fetch and spend is recorded after success. Enrich returns only the matched records, and `no_match` comes back when nothing matched or a search returns zero rows.
- **Enrich details:** the highest-`confidence_score` match wins per URL. Only city, state and country are copied from `locations`, so `street_address`, `headquarters` and `all_office_addresses` never appear in output. A test checks this.
- **Chunking:** 30 URLs go out as 25 + 5, and each chunk is checked by the guard first. If a later chunk fails after earlier ones matched, I return `ok` with the partial results. That can hide the failure, so say if you'd rather it surfaced.
- **Errors and retries:**
  - 401/403 → `auth_failed`, 400/422 → `bad_request`. Other 4xx also map to `bad_request`, which you didn't specify.
  - 429, 5xx and network errors retry with 1s then 2s waits, honouring `Retry-After` (capped at 60s). Exhausted 429s return `rate_limited`; the rest return `timeout`.
  - Messages are only "HTTP <status> <category>", and a test confirms the key never appears.
- **Cost:** search is 0.069 per record returned, enrich is 0.60 per company matched, and autocomplete is free. Each record's `cost_usd` is its own per-record price.
- **Additions beyond the spec:** I added an optional `sleep` constructor option so tests don't wait 1–2 seconds. An unreadable 200 body maps to `empty_or_partial`.
- **Smoke script:** it exits without `--confirm-spend`, takes the first industry autocomplete suggests, and prints only counts, costs and per-field non-empty counts.

content.text:
I found the root cause, and the mapper was not the problem.

**Root cause:** the saved response in `~/Desktop/neathack-data/search-sample.json` already has empty strings for `basic_info.name`, `primary_domain`, `website` and `professional_network_url` on all 3 records. I ran the old mapper over that file offline and it gave the same counts as the smoke run: 0/3 for those four fields, 3/3 for logo, size range and industry. The mapper and `crustdata-smoke.ts` both read the right fields, and the smoke script's non-empty counting is also correct.

- **Logo:** `logo_permalink` is a non-empty 127-character string on every record. I didn't print it. It is probably a placeholder or signed URL that the dashboard doesn't render as a logo.
- **Mapper:** it already handled the real shape. I still removed the guessed alternatives, so it now reads only `companies[]` and nested paths such as `basic_info.name`.
- **Tests:** I added one with every real path populated and one with only `crustdata_company_id` and `employee_count_range`. The full suite (194 tests), `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` pass.
- **Open question:** I don't know why the API returns empty fields here, or where the dashboard gets its names and LinkedIn URLs. I haven't tested whether the same request without the `fields` list fills them in; you could try one of the live calls without it.

I didn't touch `scripts/crustdata-smoke.ts`, since it had no bug, and I ran no live script.
